texts.exact_text: Hsiâo Khû indicates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and success. (We see) dense clouds, but no rain coming from our borders in the west.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 9; scan-backed transcription p. 76, hexagram statement
texts.notes: Legge's title restored from the source statement.

texts.exact_text: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject returning and pursuing his own course. What mistake should he fall into? There will be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 9; scan-backed transcription p. 76, line 1

texts.exact_text: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject, by the attraction (of the former line), returning (to the proper course). There will be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 9; scan-backed transcription p. 76, line 2

texts.exact_text: The third NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of a carriage, the strap beneath which has been removed, or of a husband and wife looking on each other with averted eyes.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 9; scan-backed transcription p. 76, line 3

texts.exact_text: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity. The danger of bloodshed is thereby averted, and his (ground for) apprehension dismissed. There will be no mistake.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 9; scan-backed transcription p. 76, line 4

texts.exact_text: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity, and drawing others to unite with him. Rich in resources, he employs his neighbours (in the same cause with himself).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 9; scan-backed transcription p. 76, line 5

texts.exact_text: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows how the rain has fallen, and the (onward progress) is stayed; -- (so) must we value the full accumulation of the virtue (represented by the upper trigram). But a wife (exercising restraint), however firm and correct she may be, is in a position of peril, (and like) the moon approaching to the full. If the superior man prosecute his measures (in such circumstances), there will be evil.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 9; scan-backed transcription p. 76, line 6

texts.exact_text:
The name Hsiâo Khû is interpreted as meaning small restraint. The idea of restraint having once been determined on as that to be conveyed by the figure, it is easily made out that the restraint must be small, for its representative is the divided line in the fourth place; and the check given by that to all the undivided lines cannot be great. Even if we suppose, as many critics do, that all the virtue of that upper trigram ☴ Xùn is concentrated in its first line, the attribute ascribed to ☴ Xùn is that of docile flexibility, which cannot long be successful against the strength emblemed by the lower trigram ☰ Qián. The restraint therefore is small, and in the end there will be 'progress and success.'

The second sentence of the Tuàn contains indications of the place, time, and personality of the writer which it seems possible to ascertain. The fief of Zhōu was the western portion of the kingdom of Yīn or Shāng, the China of the twelfth century B. C., the era of king Wén. Rain coming and moistening the ground is the cause of the beauty and luxuriance of the vegetable world, and the emblem of the blessings flowing from good training and good government. Here therefore in the west, the hereditary territory of the house of Zhōu, are blessings which might enrich the whole kingdom; but they are somehow restrained. The dense clouds do not empty their stores.

P. Regis says: -- 'To declare openly that no rain fell from the heavens long covered with dense clouds over the great tract of country, which stretched from the western border to the court and on to the eastern sea, was nothing else but leaving it to all thoughtful minds to draw the conclusion that the family of Wén was as worthy of the supreme seat as that of Shào, the tyrant, however ancient, was unworthy of it.' The intimation is not put in the Text, however, so clearly as by P. Regis.

Line 1 is undivided, the first line of ☰ Qián, occupying its proper place. Its subject, therefore, notwithstanding the check of line 4, resumes his movement, and will act according to his strong nature, and go forward.

Line 2 is also strong, and though an even place is not appropriate to it, that place being central, its subject will make common cause with the subject of line 1; and there will be good fortune.

Line 3, though strong, and in a proper place, yet not being in the centre, is supposed to be less able to resist the restraint of line 4; and hence it has the ill omens that are given.

The subject of line 4, one weak line against all the strong lines of the hexagram, might well expect wounds, and feel apprehension in trying to restrain the others; but it is in its proper place; it is the first line also of ☴ Xùn, whose attribute is docile flexibility. The strong lines are moved to sympathy and help, and there is no mistake.

Line 5 occupies the central place of ☴ Xùn, and converts, by the sincerity, of its subject, 4 and 6 into its neighbours, who suffer themselves to be used by it, and effect their common object.

In line 6, the idea of the hexagram has run its course. The harmony of nature is restored. The rain falls, and the onward march of the strong lines should now stop. But weakness that has achieved such a result, if it plume itself on it, will be in a position of peril; and like the full moon, which must henceforth wane. Let the superior man, when he has attained his end, remain in quiet. 小畜 ䷈
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 9; scan-backed transcription p. 76, notes

texts.exact_text: 小畜：亨。密雲不雨，自我西郊。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 易經卦辭

texts.exact_text: 小畜，柔得位而上下應之，曰小畜。健而巽，剛中而志行，乃亨。密雲不雨，尚往也。自我西郊，施未行也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 彖

texts.exact_text: 風行天上，小畜，君子以懿文德。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 大象

texts.exact_text: 初九：復自道，何其咎，吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 爻 1

texts.exact_text: 復自道，其義吉也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 小象 1

texts.exact_text: 九二：牽復，吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 爻 2

texts.exact_text: 牽復在中，亦不自失也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 小象 2

texts.exact_text: 九三：輿說輻，夫妻反目。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 爻 3

texts.exact_text: 夫妻反目，不能正室也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 小象 3

texts.exact_text: 六四：有孚，血去惕出，无咎。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 爻 4

texts.exact_text: 有孚。惕出。上合志也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 小象 4

texts.exact_text: 九五：有孚攣如，富以其鄰。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 爻 5

texts.exact_text: 有孚攣如，不獨富也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 小象 5

texts.exact_text: 上九：既雨既處，尚德載，婦貞厲，月幾望，君子征凶。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 爻 6

texts.exact_text: 既雨既處，德積載也。君子征凶，有所疑也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/小畜; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 9, 小象 6

texts.exact_text:
In Hsiâo Khû the weak line occupies its (proper) position, and (the lines) above and below respond to it. Hence comes the name of Hsiâo Khû (Small Restraint).

(It presents the symbols of) strength ☰ and flexibility ☴. Strong lines are in the central places, and the will (of their subjects) will have free course. Thus it indicates that there will be progress and success.

Dense clouds but no rain indicate the movement (of the strong lines) still going forward. The Commencing at our western border indicates that the (beneficial) influence has not yet been widely displayed.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix I, Hexagram 9, p. 222

texts.exact_text: (The trigram ☰ representing) the sky, and ☴ that representing wind moving above it, form Hsiâo Khû The superior man, in accordance with this, adorns the outward manifestation of his virtue.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 9, p. 279

texts.exact_text: 'He returns and pursues his own path:' -- it is right that there should be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 9, line 1, p. 279

texts.exact_text: 'By the attraction (of the subject of the former line) he returns (to its own course),' and is in the central place:--neither will he err in what is due from him.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 9, line 2, p. 279

texts.exact_text: 'Husband and wife look on each other with averted eyes:' -- (the subject of line three is like a husband who) cannot maintain correctly his relations with his wife.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 9, line 3, p. 279

texts.exact_text: 'He is possessed of sincerity; his (ground for) apprehension is dismissed:' -- (the subjects of the lines) above agree in aim with him.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 9, line 4, p. 279

texts.exact_text: 'He is possessed of sincerity, and draws others to unite with him:' -- he does not use only his own rich resources.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 9, line 5, p. 279

texts.exact_text: 'The rain has fallen and (the onward progress) is stayed:' -- the power (denoted in the figure) has accumulated to the full. 'If the superior man prosecute his measures, there will be evil:' -- he will find himself obstructed.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 9, line 6, p. 279
